page: Vultr vhp-8c-16gb-intel is an instance in the High Performance lineup, configured with 8 shared vCPUs derived from 4 physical Intel Xeon cores running at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features hyperthreading with two threads per core and incorporates 32 KB L1 data cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. Vector extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware-accelerated AES cryptography and BMI2 instruction support. System memory totals 16.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, while storage is provisioned via a bundled 350 GB local NVMe SSD. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and operates without dedicated hardware acceleration or GPUs.

Benchmark results position the instance within the mid-tier performance band across general compute and memory throughput tests, offset by lower single-threaded metrics. The system achieved a PassMark CPU score of 12,523.23 and a Stress-NG multi-core score of 11,603.93. Memory bandwidth sustains 62.89 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 44.50 GB/sec for writes. However, single-core execution reflects the modest 2.0 GHz clock speed, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,090.0 and weak multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 35.65 GB/sec. Data operations show balanced in-memory cache capability with 12.74 million Redis SET operations per second, though synthetic database operations in PassMark rated in the bottom quartile.

Resource allocation presents an advantageous balance of multi-core throughput and bundled local high-speed NVMe storage. Because the vCPUs use shared host allocation, peak sustained execution may experience contention compared to dedicated-core options, and small memory per core limits heavyweight in-memory databases. In contrast, workloads involving static web serving throughput (measured at 8.38 GB/sec), continuous integration pipelines, software compilation via Clang (scoring 10,363.0 in Geekbench), and parallelized batch jobs benefit substantially from the high thread count and responsive local storage.
description: Vultr vhp-8c-16gb-intel is a compute-oriented cloud server within the High Performance product line, featuring 8 shared vCPUs on 4 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.0 GHz, 16.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 350 GB NVMe SSD. Operating on x86_64 architecture, the processor supports AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES instructions. Benchmarks demonstrate solid mid-range multi-core efficiency, logging 5,786.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 12.74 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Conversely, single-core throughput remains modest with a Geekbench score of 1,090.0, and 7B model LLM inference registers weak responsiveness. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and integrated high-speed local NVMe storage make this instance practical for parallel compilation, CI/CD runners, distributed microservices, and static web traffic hosting.
